text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 24 in history:
1567 - Mary Queen of Scots was forced to abdicate and James VI became King of Scotland at the age of one.
1701 - Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac founded a trading post at Fort Pontchartrain, which later became the city of Detroit.
1704 - Gibraltar was captured from Spain by Admiral Sir George Rooke.
1712 - The French defeated the Allied British-Dutch forces at Denain, France, in the War of the Spanish Succession.
1775 - Eugene Francois Vidocq born. A French detective, he set up the Brigade de Surete -- the world's first detective agency.
1783 - Simon Bolivar was born in Venezuela; he freed much of South America from Spanish control and Bolivia was named after him.
1799 - Napoleon gained his last victory during his occupation of Egypt, defeating the Turks at the Battle of Aboukir.
1802 - Alexandre Dumas, French playwright and author of "The Count of Monte Cristo" and "The Three Musketeers", born.
1817 - Adolphus William, duke of Nassau, born. As grand duke of Luxembourg (from 1890), he was first ruler of the autonomous duchy.
1824 - The results of the world's first public opinion poll were published in Delaware, on voting intentions for the next U.S. presidential election.
1847 - The Convention of Gramido ended the civil war in Portugal.
1862 - Martin van Buren died; he was the eighth president of the United States and the first not to be born a British subject.
1866 - Tennessee became the first seceding state to be re-admitted to the Union.
1883 - Matthew Webb, first man to swim the English Channel (in 1875) drowned while attempting to swim the rapids above Niagara Falls
1898 - Amelia Earhart, U.S. aviator who became the first woman to cross the Atlantic by plane (in 1932), born.
1923 - The Treaty of Lausanne was signed between Turkey and the allied powers. Turkey gave up all claims to non-Turkish territories lost in the First World War.
1943 - Operation Gomorrah, the concentrated heavy bombing of Hamburg by the allies, began.
1965 - Constance Bennett, U.S. actress, died; best known for her comedies including "What Price Hollywood" and "Two Faced Woman".
1967 - President de Gaulle, visiting Montreal, made a speech which ended "Vive le Qubec libre"; he was promptly rebuked by Canadian Prime Minister Lester Pearson and cut short his visit.
1969 - Gerald Brook was released to Britain by the Soviet Union in exchange for spies Peter and Helen Kroger.
1974 - The government of Constantine Karamanlis was sworn in in Greece and a general amnesty for all political prisoners announced.
1974 - Sir James Chadwick, the English physicist who discovered the neutron and later worked on the Manhattan Project to develop the atom bomb, died.
1974 - The U.S. Supreme Court ordered President Nixon to surrender 64 White House tape recordings to the Washington District Court conducting the Watergate proceedings.
1980 - Peter Sellers, British actor and comedian, died. Noted for his film roles in "Dr Strangelove" and the "Pink Panther" movies, as well as the BBC radio series "The Goons".
1981 - Floods killed over 700 people in Szechuan province in China; 1.5 million were left homeless.
1990 - U.S. warships in the Gulf were placed on alert after Iraq massed nearly 30,000 troops near its border with Kuwait.
1993 - Russia's central bank announced a drastic reform of the monetary system, saying all banknotes issued up to the end of 1992 would be withdrawn from circulation.
1995 - A suicide bomber from the militant Moslem group Hamas blew up an Israeli bus in Tel-Aviv, killing six people and wounding 32.
1996 - 57 people were killed and more than 500 were injured when a bomb ripped through a packed commuter train in a Colombo suburb.
